description: The menu on a session row in the sessions sidebar, opened by right-click (press and hold on touch) at the pointer. Its items depend on whether the session is on this machine or on a host, its state, and whether it can be a Bot. A Bot row has the same menu.
opens: right-click a session row (not the open unsaved chat, not a ghost)

phone.does: Opened by a long-press on a session or Bot row, at the finger; Move to Group's list opens in place of the items, with a back row first

parts.name: Rename…
parts.shows: "Rename…". Shown for every session except a gone host's. Opens the Rename dialog (RenameSession.dialog.json).

actions.does: Same, on the focused or selected row.

parts.name: Bot items
parts.shows: Only for a top-level session on a host that is alive, supports Bots, and runs a model of Claude's or pi's program (not a fork): either "Make Bot…" (a plain chat) or both "Bot Settings…" and "Turn Back into a Chat" (a Bot). They sit right after Rename…, before Move to Group.

actions.does: Opens the Make Bot / Bot Settings dialog (BotSettings.dialog.json).

actions.by: click Turn Back into a Chat
actions.does: The host lists it as a plain chat again; its memory and picture stay on the host for if it is made a Bot again.

parts.name: Move to Group
parts.shows: A submenu, for any chat (this machine's or a host's), after Rename… and any Bot items (first if there is no Rename…). Lists each group by name (those made, those chats are put in, and those hosts' sessions were started in), alphabetical, the chat's own ticked; then "No Group"; then, in a separate section, "New Group…".

actions.by: click a group or No Group
actions.does: Puts the chat in that group (or none); the list and the ⋮ → Groups list refresh. Undo is not offered.
Asks for a name (GroupName.dialog.json); the group is made and this chat moved into it.

parts.name: Archive / Unarchive
parts.shows: "Archive" for a normal session, "Unarchive" for one that is already archived (here, in Claude Desktop, or on its host). For a session on a host that is at a turn (working or waiting), Archive is left out (Stop is offered instead). For a session of this machine's own: archived only in Baude's settings, listed under Archived. On a host: archived there, for every app.

actions.does: Moves it to the Archived group (or back). An archived chat is read-only, its text box gone, until it's unarchived (MenuActions, Read-only session). A host that refuses says "<host> didn't archive it: <why>" / "…didn't unarchive it: <why>" in a toast.

parts.name: Stop
parts.shows: Only for a session on a host that is working or waiting (and not gone): "Stop".

actions.does: Stops its claude (its host keeps the session to carry on with).

parts.name: Move to Trash…
parts.shows: "Move to Trash…" Opens the confirmation (MoveToTrash.dialog.json). Not shown for a session on a gone host (see Delete).

parts.name: Delete
parts.shows: Only for a session whose host is gone (dead) or not alive: the sole item: "Delete". Its transcript is the host's, so it's only hidden from the list until it shows up again (used since, at a turn, or its host back); Archive keeps a session out for good.

actions.does: The session is hidden from the list; if it's the open chat, a new session opens in its place.

states.name: this machine's session (plain)
states.shows: Rename…, Move to Group ▸, Archive (or Unarchive), Move to Trash…. Order: Rename…, Move to Group, Archive, Move to Trash….

states.name: host session, idle
states.shows: Rename…, [Make Bot… | Bot Settings… and Turn Back into a Chat], Move to Group ▸, Archive, Move to Trash….

states.name: host session, working or waiting
states.shows: Rename…, Move to Group ▸, Stop, Move to Trash… (no Archive; an archived one at a turn shows Unarchive).

states.name: host session, host gone
states.shows: Move to Group ▸, Delete. (Rename… is absent.)

states.name: host session, deactivated
states.shows: As gone: Move to Group ▸, Delete.

removed.name: Give Mesh Tools / Remove Mesh Tools
removed.why: Mesh tools are not handed to chats one by one: a Bot has them and Meta has them, always, and no other chat does
